title: A relative H1-regular immersion over a locally finitely presented base is flat on a neighbourhood of its image and is a regular immersion stable under base change

standard_prerequisites.name: The approximation of a flat and finitely presented algebra by a flat algebra of finite type over a finitely generated ring, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the Noetherian model over which the quotient by the chosen sequence is flat.

standard_prerequisites.name: Surjectivity of the base change map on the first Koszul cohomology of a sequence, and exactness of directed colimits, both cited from the algebra and more-algebra chapters
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the finitely many generators of the Koszul cohomology of the model be killed after a further finitely generated extension of the base ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness descends along the base change defining the model, cited from the morphisms chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the flatness statement obtained for the model back to the original morphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: A quasi-regular immersion is flat at each point of its image, and the flat locus of a finite type morphism of Noetherian schemes is open, cited from the same chapter and the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies pointwise flatness in the reduced situation and turns it into an open neighbourhood.

standard_prerequisites.name: A relative regular immersion which is flat in a neighbourhood of its image is a regular immersion with the property stable under base change, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives part (2) once part (1) is known.

core_obligations: Reduce to the affine local case: at a point of the closed subscheme it is enough to produce an open neighbourhood on which the morphism to the base is flat, and locally the immersion is given by an H1-regular sequence in a finitely presented algebra over the base ring whose quotient is flat (proof lines 5408-5416).

Build a Noetherian model: write the algebra as a quotient of a polynomial algebra, lift the chosen sequence, choose a finitely generated subring of the base containing all coefficients, form the corresponding model algebra and sequence, and observe that the original algebra and its quotient by the sequence are obtained by base change; then enlarge the subring so that the quotient of the model is flat over it (proof lines 5418-5429).

Kill the first Koszul cohomology of the model: that group is a finitely generated module over the Noetherian model, so choose finitely many generators; for any larger finitely generated extension of the base ring the base change map on the first Koszul cohomology is surjective, and the colimit of the corresponding complexes is the complex of the original sequence, which is acyclic in degree one by hypothesis; exactness of directed colimits makes the colimit of the cohomology groups vanish, so some extension kills all the chosen generators, making the first Koszul cohomology of that model vanish (proof lines 5430-5455).

Descend to the Noetherian finite type case: the model and its closed subscheme base change to the original ones, so it suffices to prove the flatness statement there by the cited descent of flatness (proof lines 5457-5466).

Finish: in the Noetherian finite type situation the morphism is flat at every point of the closed subscheme, and the flat locus is open, which gives part (1); part (2) follows from the cited statement on relative regular immersions that are flat in a neighbourhood (proof lines 5468-5477).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine local situation with an H1-regular sequence and spread the data out to a finitely generated model over which the quotient is flat (proof lines 5408-5429).

Kill the obstruction in the first Koszul cohomology by enlarging the model, descend flatness back along the base change, and conclude with openness of the flat locus plus the neighbourhood criterion for relative regular immersions (proof lines 5430-5477).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a relative H1-regular immersion into a base that is locally of finite presentation, the ambient scheme is flat over the base on a neighbourhood of the closed subscheme, and the immersion is in fact a regular immersion whose regularity persists under arbitrary base change (statement lines 5395-5406). The counted proof is a substantial Noetherian approximation argument: after reducing to an affine local situation with an H1-regular sequence whose quotient is flat, it spreads the algebra, the sequence and the flatness out to a finitely generated model, kills the finitely generated first Koszul cohomology of that model by enlarging the base ring (using surjectivity of the base change map on Koszul cohomology and exactness of directed colimits), descends flatness back along the base change, and finishes with openness of the flat locus and the neighbourhood criterion for relative regular immersions (proof lines 5408-5477). It is H2: the approximation layer is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard approximation, Koszul and flatness statements.
